verdict.rationale: Honeycomb Triggers and SLO burn alerts let users define threshold rules that fire automatically and send JSON payloads to Slack, PagerDuty, Teams, or a custom webhook. Payloads can be customized with variables and Go template functions, and triggers can be managed through the API and MCP tools. The only automatic action documented, though, is delivering an alert notification or webhook. Rules evaluate thresholds on query results rather than arbitrary events, and there is no native action or workflow engine. Missing for 10: built-in automated actions beyond alert delivery, rule conditions on arbitrary events, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Use triggers to send alerts when thresholds that you define and configure are passed.
Set up Triggers and SLOs to alert your team when conditions are met, and route notifications to Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, or a custom webhook.
Once configured, Honeycomb sends JSON payloads to your webhook upon alerts firing.
Programmatically manage datasets, queries, triggers, SLOs, environments, API keys, and more.
